key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in MAPbI3 precursor inks depends strongly on the specific halide precursor, with I2/polyiodides degrading MXene, PbI2 oxidizing it more slowly, and MAI helping stabilize the flakes.
engineering_relevance: MXene additives in perovskite processing must be selected and mixed in a controlled order to avoid unwanted chemical degradation and to tune interfacial chemistry for better device integration.
method: XPS tracked surface composition and oxidation state changes after exposure to individual ink components.
DFT calculations explained how each precursor interacts with MXene terminations.
Comparative analysis separated the roles of I2/polyiodides, PbI2, and MAI in MXene aging.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports combined XPS and DFT evidence showing rapid degradation from iodine species, slower PbI2-driven oxidation, and MAI-induced passivation of Ti3C2Tx.
watch_item: Precursor addition order can change the final MXene surface state, so processing protocols must be tightly controlled to prevent unintended degradation.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
